headline: Why good talent is no longer enough
summary: As Newgen Software shifts toward becoming an AI-led product business, CHRO Kashish Kapoor emphasizes that organizations must prioritize helping existing employees stay adaptable and commercially aware rather than relying solely on new hires. The discussion highlights that effective capability building requires HR to align learning programs directly with strategic business outcomes and local market contexts.

headline: UP hikes panchayat assistants’ pay by 50%
summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has raised the monthly honorarium for over 57,000 panchayat assistants by 50%, increasing it from Rs 6,000 to Rs 9,000 following recent protests. In addition to the salary hike, the state introduced workplace protections including Direct Benefit Transfer for timely payments, maternity leave, and stricter termination safeguards. These policy changes successfully resolved long-standing grievances and led to the end of the grassroots demonstration.

headline: Case-in-Point: The forced fun culture
summary: Synapse Technologies' CEO credits the firm's low attrition rate to a highly social corporate culture centered around frequent team outings and retreats. However, HR has received complaints from employees who feel overwhelmed or excluded by the implicit expectation to attend these events. The company now faces a dilemma on whether to redesign its social participation model or offer accommodations without undermining team cohesion.

headline: Amazon raises UK frontline pay by up to 5.6%, covering 70,000 employees
summary: Amazon is increasing starting wages by up to 5.6% for approximately 70,000 UK frontline employees, bringing hourly pay to between £15.10 and £16.10 alongside enhanced benefits. The wage expansion aligns with the company's broader £40 billion UK investment plan set through 2027. Concurrently, Amazon India is adding over 160,000 seasonal workers across 400 cities to support surging e-commerce demand ahead of the festive season.

headline: Disney moves to full enforcement of four-day office mandate
summary: The Walt Disney Company is strictly enforcing its four-day in-office mandate, eliminating remaining remote work exceptions for product and technology employees. Non-compliant staff now face potential termination as company leadership moves to standardize attendance and strengthen in-person collaboration. This heightened enforcement aligns Disney with other major corporations like BlackRock and Snap in scaling back pandemic-era remote work policies.

headline: Arete Group expands employee wellbeing focus through UMatter programme
summary: Arete Group has expanded its focus on employee mental health through the launch of its UMatter workplace wellbeing programme, developed in partnership with MindPeers. The initiative provides confidential counselling and uses awareness campaigns to position mental wellbeing as a core business priority rather than a standard benefit. By fostering open dialogue and leadership advocacy, Arete aims to create a supportive workplace culture that encourages early intervention.

headline: Engineers make up 42% of Vedanta workforce as group focuses on industrial skills
summary: Engineers now account for 42% of Vedanta Group's workforce, covering traditional disciplines like mining and metallurgy alongside emerging areas such as AI, robotics, and data science. The conglomerate recruits from top technical institutes and leverages internal mobility to deploy talent across its metals, power, and oil and gas operations. This dual emphasis on core engineering and modern digital skills aims to drive automation, sustainability, and operational efficiency across its business units.

headline: Wells Fargo fires employees over mouse jiggler use to simulate work activity
summary: Wells Fargo recently discharged more than a dozen employees after an internal review revealed they were using technology to simulate keyboard and mouse activity. The incident underscores the growing reliance on digital surveillance tools in hybrid work environments and highlights the limitations of tracking activity metrics rather than actual productivity.

headline: How V-Estate turned real estate sales entirely digital
summary: L&T Realty partnered with proptech firm V-Estate to eliminate physical show flats for its Ahana residential project in Mumbai, transitioning entirely to a digital sales gallery. The immersive experience utilizes holographic masterplans, Unreal Engine previews, and Meta Quest VR headsets to provide hyper-realistic unit views and interactive floor plans. The initiative successfully achieved universal buyer adoption across all demographics, proving that real estate developers can significantly cut construction costs through digital-first sales strategies.
